name: coding
description: Maintain a small invoicing library: fix bugs, add features under team conventions given early, then recall decisions.

turns.prompt: I'm taking over the ledgerline package in this directory. Read every file under src/ and test/ and give me a five-bullet overview of how it is organised.

Team conventions you must follow for the rest of this session: (a) every thrown error is a LedgerError whose code starts with `LL_` followed by SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE, e.g. LL_UNKNOWN_REGION; (b) money is always integer cents, never floats; (c) every new exported function gets a one-line JSDoc comment. Acknowledge in one sentence.
Run the test suite and tell me which tests fail and why.
Fix the failing tax test without changing the test itself, then run the tax tests again.
We now invoice customers in Luxembourg and Austria. Add LU with a VAT rate of 17% and AT with 20%.
taxFor silently returns 0 for regions we don't know, which hid a bug last month. Make it throw a LedgerError instead, following our error-code convention (unknown region).
Show me how totals() in src/invoice.js computes the numbers, step by step, and point out anything that looks fragile.
The CSV export breaks when a customer name or description contains a comma or a double quote. Fix toCsv so it follows RFC 4180 quoting.
Add a test for the CSV quoting to test/csv.test.js (a customer with a comma and a description with double quotes) and run the whole suite.

Here is the finance team's spec. Compare our implementation against it and list the gaps; don't change code yet.

{{truth.financeSpec}}

Finance gave us two discount codes: WELCOME10 is 10% off and FIXED500 is a fixed 500 cents off. Create src/discounts.js exporting applyDiscount(invoice, code), which returns a new invoice with the code recorded on it. An unknown code must throw following our convention (unknown discount).

Now update totals() so it returns { subtotal, discount, tax, total } per the finance spec: the discount applies before tax, VAT is computed per line on the discounted line amount, and a fixed discount is spread over the lines with allocate() from money.js. Keep existing callers working.
Run the suite and fix whatever broke.
Add tests for discounts: WELCOME10, FIXED500 on a multi-line invoice, and an unknown code.
Per the spec, quantities must be positive integers. Make createInvoice and addLine throw on anything else, using our convention with the code suffix INVALID_LINE, and add a test.
Add summary(invoice) to src/invoice.js returning { lines, subtotal, discount, tax, total, currency } and export it from src/index.js. Follow our documentation convention.

Quick check from memory: which VAT rate did we set for Luxembourg, and which prefix must our error codes use? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
From memory: list every file you created or modified in this session. Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
Write a CHANGELOG.md with a 0.3.0 entry that covers everything we changed this session.
From memory: which code is the fixed discount and how many cents does it take off? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
Bump package.json to version 0.3.0, run the full test suite one last time and report the pass/fail counts.

From memory: which two existing bugs did we fix before adding features (one short phrase each)? Do not open files or run shell commands for this; memory tools are fine if you have them. Answer in one line.
